content: No, this is not true. According to Swiss law, to apply for Swiss naturalization, a person generally needs to have resided in Switzerland for a minimum of 10 years of legal residency (continuously or cumulatively) after turning 10 years old. This applies to most cantons and is a federal requirement. However, the type of residence permit (such as a B permit) does not reduce the required residency period for naturalization. Additional requirements include integration, knowledge of the local language, and no significant criminal record. Always check with the local municipality or canton for specific details, as naturalization requirements can vary slightly by canton.
